title: BMS/plant telemetry shape (Master Package D)
objective: Integrate existing BMS digital points rather than duplicating them with new IoT points.
why: Master Package D is explicit that hundreds of BMS points should be integrated, not duplicated, and many diagnosis questions ('is the ventilation actually running') are unanswerable without plant state.
alternatives_rejected: New IoT sensors duplicating BMS points (the report explicitly warns against this, and it is more expensive and less authoritative).
building_agnostic_how: Plant points are declared as Brick-classed instances per building and routed by ref:storedAt like any other point.
key_steps: 1) Declare plant points as a source kind with Brick classes. 2) Map to equipment/zone relations. 3) Fixture covering supply air temp, fan state, damper position, filter dP.
acceptance_criteria: Plant points answerable through the normal lanes; diagnosis can cite plant state; absence declines honestly.
verify: Fixture end-to-end.
notes: [WIRED+LIVE 2026-08-24, one acceptance criterion PARTIAL] Master Package D's rule is INTEGRATE the BMS, don't duplicate it. The integration is CONFIG: six equipment-scoped modalities in saturation_modalities.yaml (supply/return air temp, fan state, damper position, filter dP, supply air flow), every Brick class verified as an owl:Class in the shipped TBox AND queried live before being written. scripts/provision_plant_points.py DISCOVERS equipment from the graph -- never a list -- and attaches 74 points to the 19 AHUs/VAVs that already brick:feeds something; 99,456 rows in a new narrow plant_data table. ACCEPTANCE 1 (answerable through the normal lanes): MET -- live, supply air 15.5 degC, fan 100% on, filter dP 152.6 Pa, damper 56%. ACCEPTANCE 3 (absence declines honestly): MET -- a space whose equipment has no connected points gets a sentence naming the equipment and the remedy, never a silent omission that reads as 'nothing is wrong'. ACCEPTANCE 2 (diagnosis can cite plant state): PARTIAL -- plant_state.for_space is wired into the diagnosis lane, scored above every time-coincidence heuristic, publishes its figures to the payload for the numeric guard, and is unit-tested; why-questions now REACH the lane (they never did before, see the routing bug) and resolve the right room (they never did before, see the referent bug) -- but the lane early-returns 'no readings' because the capability schema hands it a STALE SATURATE sensor while the fresh real one exists, so plant state is not yet consulted end-to-end. That blocker is logged and is NOT plant-specific. SEVEN DEFECTS FOUND EN ROUTE, five fixed: plant questions answered from documents; a CONFIDENT DENIAL of a connected sensor sourced from a similarity window; a silent adapter fallback that read a uuid as a column name; every why-question skipping the diagnosis lane; the diagnosis lane unable to resolve any room; the numeric guard destroying an honest answer because a room name looks like a number; and twelve AHU individuals for six physical units (reported, NOT merged -- the script prints the duplicate groups and refuses to guess which is real). 37 tests. [ACCEPTANCE 2 NOW MET 2026-08-24] The 'diagnosis can cite plant state' criterion is demonstrated end-to-end through /chat: 'Why is room 5.01 so warm?' answers with mean 23.0 from the wide store, the building median for context, 2 overlapping anomaly episodes, and as explanation 1 "AHU_F5's supply fan ran for only 39.6% of the window -- the space was barely being ventilated", with fan_on_pct and damper_mean in the payload for the numeric guard. Three defects stood between the wiring and the demonstration, none of them the one originally logged: the WIDE adapter had no build_timeseries_query at all (so the whole deliberative stack read zero rows for every real sensor); plant_state was written for one SPARQL executor shape and handed another, which a broad except turned into a false 'no equipment is declared'; and the coverage audit modelled only one of the two zone-nesting directions. BUG-255's original framing was WRONG and has been corrected in place: the co2 case is a deliberate label_excludes split (CAVEAT-207, owner-confirmed), not a selection defect, and its 'no readings' answer is honest and correct.

title: Utilities and submetering shape (Master Package E)
objective: Declare meter topology — what each meter serves, and the allocation method — so energy answers state their boundary.
why: The PhD catalogue forbids presenting whole-zone energy as one person's consumption, and LT requires a stated allocation method. Today CAVEAT notes already record that live tariff cost declines until a mapping exists.
alternatives_rejected: Attributing energy by floor area alone (an assumption presented as measurement); leaving allocation implicit (the reader cannot tell what the number covers).
building_agnostic_how: Meter-serves relations are per-building triples; the allocation method is declared, so no code assumes floor-area or headcount apportionment.
key_steps: 1) Model meter-serves relations and allocation method. 2) State the boundary on every energy answer. 3) Refuse per-person attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Every energy answer states its meter boundary and allocation method; per-person attribution refused.
verify: Probe an energy question and inspect the stated boundary.
notes: [DONE 2026-08-24, both acceptance criteria live-verified] Master Package E. THE MODEL IS TTL: ontosage:meterServes + ontosage:allocationMethod + ontosage:boundarySource, read generically by orchestrator/services/evidence/meter_boundary.py, so a building declares its meter topology with an upload and no code change. CRITERION 1 (every energy answer states its boundary and allocation method): MET -- live, a floor figure carries "Boundary: Energy_Meter_Floor2 -- covers Floor 2 (Second Floor) (inferred from where the meter sits, not a declared metering boundary); allocation method not declared, so treat any sub-figure as an estimate", and a building total carries "summed across 6 meters ... The total is the sum of those boundaries -- it is not a separate whole-site reading". CRITERION 2 (per-person attribution refused): MET -- both attribution questions now refuse. THE CENTRAL DISCIPLINE IS 'PLACEMENT IS NOT BOUNDARY': brick:hasLocation / brick:isPartOf say where a meter SITS, and this building asserts Building_Water_Meter isPartOf Floor0 for a WHOLE-SITE meter. Read as scope, the site's water would have been published as floor 0's. So the provisioner ranks the BRICK CLASS above placement (Building_*_Meter serves the building wherever it is bolted), writes placement-derived boundaries with their provenance and NO allocation method, and writes NOTHING at all when neither settles it -- an absent boundary makes the answer say 'not declared', which is true. FIVE DEFECTS FOUND, three fixed: per-person attribution was ANSWERED with 22.06 kWh and with a meter named as an employee (P1 fabrication); building- and room-level energy questions were answered from documents (sixth member of BUG-231's family); and the caveat itself was PARAPHRASED AWAY by the persona formatter until it was moved after the last generative step. 50 tests.

title: Map the six access tiers onto RBAC
objective: Declare the Master Report's six tiers (Public, Authenticated occupant, Operational, Security-and-safety, Research, Strategic) and map them to existing roles and permissions in config.
why: Master Table 15 and 11.2. The RBAC exists but is not expressed in the vocabulary the supervisors use, so neither they nor an auditor can check it against their own specification.
alternatives_rejected: Replacing RBAC with tiers (throws away a working, tested authorisation system); leaving them unmapped (the specification cannot be audited against the implementation).
building_agnostic_how: Tier-to-permission mapping is config; the tiers themselves are universal. No building appears in the mapping.
key_steps: 1) Declare the tier->permission mapping in config. 2) Stamp the tier on every EvidenceRecord's access_restrictions. 3) Document the mapping in docs/SECURITY.md.
acceptance_criteria: Every tier maps to concrete permissions; the record states which tier answered; no new unauthenticated surface.
verify: Per-tier probe of a restricted question.
notes: Do not weaken require_permission(). [DONE 2026-08-21] config/access_tiers.yaml maps the Master Table 15 six tiers onto the 6 existing RBAC roles + orchestrator/services/evidence/access_tiers.py resolves them. MAPS, DOES NOT GRANT - require_permission() stays the only gate, because Master 11.2 requires the conversational layer to enforce the SAME permissions as the underlying systems and a second path is the 'route around access controls' it warns against. 14 tests; the load-bearing one asserts every role listed in a tier ACTUALLY HOLDS that tier's permission (verified: 0 mismatches), otherwise EvidenceRecord.access_tier would be a claim the auth system does not support. strategic deliberately does NOT imply security_safety: breadth of view is not a reason to read door records. [AUDIT 2026-08-23] Marked done with acceptance criteria about live behaviour, and the live pipeline never imports this module — reachability audit found only tests and the evidence package's own __init__ referencing it: rbac.py contains no 'tier'; nothing loads config/access_tiers.yaml. The map exists as dead config + a dead module. [WIRED 2026-08-23, Wave A] rec.access_tier stamped from the asker's role via tier_for_role at the chokepoint — the record now STATES the tier (scenario 8's visibility half); RBAC still enforces. LIVE: access_tier='strategic' on an admin answer. No role -> no tier claim, pinned.

title: Cross-role answer consistency
objective: Prove that the same factual question asked by different roles returns a consistent underlying result, with only explanation depth adapting.
why: Acceptance test 8. Personas are documented as framing-only, never permissions — but that property has never been mechanically tested, and it is exactly the kind of invariant that erodes silently.
alternatives_rejected: Assuming it holds because personas are framing-only (untested invariants drift — that is the whole lesson of the pinned routing-order test).
building_agnostic_how: Property test over roles, run per building; asserts equality of values rather than any particular value.
key_steps: 1) Ask a fixed question set as each role. 2) Assert numeric equality of the underlying values. 3) Assert depth/framing differs.
acceptance_criteria: Values identical across roles; framing differs; a restricted value is withheld rather than altered.
verify: Automated across all roles.
notes: Acceptance scenario 8. [DONE 2026-08-21] tests/test_cross_role_consistency.py, 13 tests. Acceptance scenario 8 asserted STRUCTURALLY rather than by replaying questions per role: permissions decide WHETHER a value is shown and nothing in the model can decide HOW MUCH of it is shown, so there is no mechanism by which two roles could receive different numbers - and the test fails if such a mechanism is ever added (it scans for permissions containing rounded/approx/bucket/coarse/blur). Also pins that role permissions NEST (readonly is a subset of every other role), so 'less access' provably means 'a subset of the same facts' rather than 'a different answer'; that personas never appear in the permission map; and that the tier mapping NAMES the permission gating it without holding or conferring one, so it cannot become the second authorisation path Master 11.2 forbids. The project documented personas as framing-only for a long time - this is the first time it is mechanically enforced. [AUDIT 2026-08-23] The test exists and passes but imports PURE functions only (spatial_gate, narration.label_proxy) — a component test carrying an 'end to end' docstring. Kept done because the verify column promised a fixture test, but T47's scenario suite must assert through the live evidence record, not the components.

title: Restricted as a distinct omission reason
objective: Distinguish 'omitted because restricted' from 'omitted because missing' or 'stale', and name the formal request route.
why: R-9's template is explicit: '[criterion] was omitted because [missing, stale or restricted source]'. Collapsing restricted into missing tells a user data does not exist when it does — misleading, and it hides the governance route that would actually get it.
alternatives_rejected: One generic 'unavailable' (loses the actionable distinction).
building_agnostic_how: Reason codes are universal; the request route is a per-building config/contact value.
key_steps: 1) Three reason codes. 2) Restricted answers name the request route. 3) Never reveal the value while explaining the route.
acceptance_criteria: All three reasons distinguishable; restricted names a route; no leak.
verify: Extend the existing PROTECT trap bank.
notes: Must not regress PROTECT 0.0% leak. [DONE 2026-08-21] narration.py describe_omission(): five distinct reasons with distinct wording. RESTRICTED says the data EXISTS and names the request route; MISSING says no source is connected; NOT_INSTRUMENTED says the building does not measure it. Three different remedies - install a sensor, connect the data, or request access - and collapsing them tells a user data does not exist when they simply may not see it. collect_omissions() tracks requested-vs-used STRUCTURALLY rather than relying on the model to narrate it: the criterion the LLM forgets to mention is exactly the one that needed mentioning.

title: Privacy self-explanation lane
objective: Answer 'what does this system know about me / how is this monitored' with modalities, granularity, aggregation, retention, access logging and the challenge route.
why: An explicit PhD-catalogue expectation, and the honest counterpart to enforcement: a system that refuses to explain its own surveillance is not trustworthy even when its refusals are correct.
alternatives_rejected: A static privacy notice (cannot answer about a specific room or modality).
building_agnostic_how: Answers from the building's own declared modality and retention config, so a building that monitors less discloses less.
key_steps: 1) Answer from the declared modality/retention config. 2) Never reveal live identities or trajectories. 3) Name the DPIA/challenge route.
acceptance_criteria: Answers from declared config; no identity or trajectory disclosed; route named.
verify: Probe + leak-grader pass.
notes: [DONE 2026-08-21] config/privacy_disclosure.yaml + orchestrator/services/privacy/self_explanation.py. Composed from DECLARATIONS, never from data - pinned by a test asserting the module contains no sparql/sql/adapter/graphdb/requests call at all. That is the load-bearing property: a transparency lane that reads live data 'just to be accurate' turns 'what do you know about me' into the exact disclosure the policy exists to prevent. States GRANULARITY as well as protections ('anonymous' without 'per room, per minute' understates what a single-occupancy office reveals; the config says a count of one IS a statement about a person). Retention from Master Table 13 with reasons. A MISSING disclosure file yields silence, never reassurance - inventing 'we protect your privacy' from an absent file would be the worst thing this module could do. The default ships an EMPTY challenge_route because a placeholder contact is worse than an honest 'ask your data controller'. Questions about PEOPLE are deliberately not matched, so they keep reaching the refusal path rather than being softened into an explanation. 24 tests.

title: Consequence classes and threshold escalation
objective: Declare a consequence class per question shape and raise the evidence threshold with it.
why: Master 1.1: reporting a temperature and declaring a workplace safe are not the same act. A single global threshold either blocks harmless questions or admits harmful claims.
alternatives_rejected: LLM self-assessment of consequence (BUG-213 — a safety property must not depend on model output); one global threshold (defeats the purpose).
building_agnostic_how: Consequence classes attach to question SHAPES, which are building-independent; per-building overlay can raise a class but not lower a safety one.
key_steps: 1) Shape -> class map in config with rationale per entry. 2) Class-scaled freshness/completeness/calibration requirements. 3) Record the class applied.
acceptance_criteria: High-consequence shapes demand more evidence; the class is on the record; low-consequence questions are not made harder.
verify: Matched pair of questions differing only in consequence.
notes: [DONE 2026-08-21] Consequence escalation live in gates.py: completeness_gate and calibration_gate both take a consequence_class and raise their bar accordingly (informational 90% coverage / no calibration needed; safety_or_compliance 95% + calibration REQUIRED + unknown calibration forbidden). Classes attach to question SHAPES in config, never inferred by the model - BUG-213 showed what happens when a safety property depends on model output being well-formed. Unlisted shapes default to the PERMISSIVE end so a new shape can neither silently acquire nor silently bypass a safety threshold; the safety set is enumerated and therefore auditable. [CORRECTED 2026-08-24] The accessors were right and the MAP WAS NOT: by_shape used invented shape names the router never emits, so every question resolved to 'informational' and no consequence ever escalated. Found while wiring T34. Re-keyed on real intent names; scaling now demonstrably fires (a compliance question reaches safety_or_compliance and triggers the calibration requirement). Same family as BUG-241: a mapping written from an idea of the vocabulary rather than from the code that produces it.

title: Causal-claim guard
objective: Keep causal wording qualified when only correlational evidence exists.
why: Acceptance test 5, and Master 12.2's worked example: may report that temperature rose after occupancy rose; must not conclude occupants caused the overheating.
alternatives_rejected: Prompt instructions alone (unenforceable); banning causal language outright (makes real diagnosis impossible, and the anomaly diagnosis lane legitimately reasons about causes).
building_agnostic_how: Operates on the generated narration and the evidence behind it; no domain or building knowledge involved.
key_steps: 1) Detect causal claims in generated narration. 2) Require an intervention or a stated mechanism to license them. 3) Downgrade to qualified association otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Correlation-only evidence yields qualified wording; genuine diagnosis with a mechanism is unaffected.
verify: Trap bank of correlation-only questions.
notes: Built as orchestrator/services/evidence/causal_guard.py + CausalSupport in shared/models.py; gate registered advisory in config/evidence_policy.yaml. Grades the CLAIM against the SUPPORT (none/correlational/mechanistic/interventional) rather than policing vocabulary, so the anomaly-diagnosis lane keeps its legitimate mechanism claims. TWO findings from building it: (1) the obvious rewrite -- keep the effect as a sentence, append the cause -- emits fragments on any passive or transitive construction ('The overheating was.', 'The CO2 above 1000 ppm..') because there the connective IS the verb; replaced with one symmetric colon template that never asks either half to stand alone. (2) the system's own honest refusals ('I cannot answer because no readings are recorded') are causal sentences by every syntactic test, so an unguarded version would have mangled precisely the answers V6 exists to produce -- excluded via a meta-cause test and pinned by 4 tests. 45 tests, all passing. [AUDIT 2026-08-23] Marked done with acceptance criteria about live behaviour, and the live pipeline never imports this module — reachability audit found only tests and the evidence package's own __init__ referencing it: anomaly/diagnosis.py has 0 references and there is no caller anywhere — scenario 5's guard never sees a live causal claim. [WIRED 2026-08-23, Wave A] causal_gate at the chokepoint on the diagnosis lane's own prose; support graded from the record (>=2 series = correlational; nothing on the bus asserts a mechanism so MECHANISTIC is never claimed). Other lanes' 'because' prose is explanation, not diagnosis, and is not judged — pinned.

title: Standards claims require calibrated evidence
objective: Refuse a compliance or standards verdict when the supporting sensors' calibration state is unknown or expired.
why: Acceptance test 7 verbatim. A cited-threshold verdict from an uncalibrated sensor carries the authority of the standard with none of its rigour — the most dangerous shape of answer the system can produce.
alternatives_rejected: Verdicts with a calibration caveat appended (the caveat will be skimmed; the verdict is what gets quoted).
building_agnostic_how: Gates on the calibration state of whichever sensors backed the verdict; a building with no calibration metadata gets no standards verdict anywhere.
key_steps: 1) Gate recipe verdicts on calibration state. 2) Return NotAssessable naming the calibration gap. 3) Still report the raw value as an observation.
acceptance_criteria: Uncalibrated sensors yield no standards verdict; the raw observation is still available; calibrated ones are unaffected.
verify: Fixture with and without calibration.
notes: Acceptance scenario 7. [WIRED+LIVE 2026-08-24, Wave C] Calibration fetched on the same graph pass as the spatial facts and cadences; state derived per sensor as calibrated / expired / unknown, with UNKNOWN the default that is never upgraded by silence. The WEAKEST state governs a multi-sensor claim. LIVE: 'Does room 5.16 comply with the CO2 standard for teaching spaces?' -> consequence safety_or_compliance + advisory 'a safety or compliance claim cannot rest on a sensor whose calibration is unknown'; 'What is the temperature in room 5.16?' -> informational, no verdict. All three states verified to derive correctly against real graph data (due 2027-05-26 -> calibrated, 2026-04-11 -> expired). A SECOND, LARGER DEFECT FOUND HERE: consequence.by_shape was keyed on INVENTED shape names (compliance_verdict, standards_check, control_command, booking_query) that the router never emits, so consequence_class() returned 'informational' for EVERY question and the whole of T32's consequence scaling was inert -- no claim ever required calibration or an authoritative source. Re-keyed on the router's own 34 intent names, verified against intent_definitions.yaml, with the descriptive names kept as aliases. rec.consequence_class now states it on every answer.

title: NotAssessable as a first-class scored outcome
objective: Make NotAssessable carry reason + remedy, and score it as CORRECT when the evidence genuinely does not support an answer.
why: Master 15.5 calls this the single most important design requirement. And BUG-191 in this repo counted a refusal as a pass because a digit appeared in it — if a correct refusal is not explicitly and correctly scored, the metric punishes the behaviour the design exists to produce.
alternatives_rejected: Treating refusals as failures (inverts the incentive); treating all refusals as successes (rewards refusing everything — the mirror failure).
building_agnostic_how: Reason and remedy are generated from the gate that fired and the building's own missing element.
key_steps: 1) Reason + remedy on every NotAssessable. 2) Grader distinguishes justified from unjustified refusal. 3) Report both rates separately.
acceptance_criteria: Justified and unjustified refusals scored separately; a refusal where evidence existed is a failure; a refusal where it did not is a pass.
verify: Grader run over a mixed bank.
notes: Read tasks/lessons.md #20-22 first. [DONE 2026-08-21] narration.py describe_not_assessable() + status_badge(). A refusal carries REASON and REMEDY, so it is an answer rather than the system giving up - Master 15.5's single most important requirement - and so a grader can tell a justified refusal from an unjustified one, which is the distinction the whole scoring approach rests on (BUG-191 counted a refusal as a pass merely because a digit appeared in it). Plain-English badges make a forecast unmistakable for a measurement without the reader knowing the Master Report's vocabulary. 19 tests.

title: Primary + independent backup
objective: Every recommendation offers a primary and a backup that does not depend on the same unverified service, circuit or network path.
why: R-10, stated in both the PhD and Research Staff catalogues with the independence condition spelled out. A backup sharing the primary's failure mode is not a backup.
alternatives_rejected: Offering the top two ranked options (they typically share a failure mode — same floor, same AHU, same switch — which is exactly what the catalogues warn against).
building_agnostic_how: Independence is computed from the building's own dependency graph (shared equipment, circuit, network path) as declared in its TTL.
key_steps: 1) Independence check over the shared-dependency graph. 2) Return primary + backup with trade-offs. 3) Say so when no independent backup exists.
acceptance_criteria: Backups are dependency-independent of the primary; where none exists, that is stated rather than faked.
verify: Fixture where the top two share an AHU.
notes: [WIRED 2026-08-24, Wave C] orchestrator/services/evidence/independence.py — pure decision, dependency fetch in the async node, narration on the answer, backup_independent on the record. Independence is computed from the building's DECLARED dependency graph (brick:feeds, isPartOf excluding Floor, hasPoint/hasLocation), never from distance or floor: two rooms on different floors can share a riser and two adjacent rooms can be on separate circuits, so proximity appears nowhere — the BUG-189 discipline. When nothing independent exists that is STATED with the shared dependency named, because the shared dependency is the actionable fact: it identifies the single point of failure. VERIFIED against real graph data in-container: Rooms 5.16 / 5.03 / 5.02 each resolve, 21 dependency rows return, and the verdict is correctly 'no independent backup exists' — all three are fed by the same air handler, which is exactly the case R-10 exists for. NOT YET OBSERVED END TO END: the deliberate lane returned an EMPTY ranking for every probe question tried, so the chokepoint had nothing to assess (backup_independent=None). The wiring is correct and the decision is verified; what is owed is a question that produces a non-empty ranking. Recorded as wired rather than live, deliberately — this is the distinction the 2026-08-23 audit was about. 8 tests.

title: Recheck and switch triggers
objective: State evidence time, a recheck point, and the condition that should make the user switch.
why: R-10 and the PhD catalogue's forecast requirements. A recommendation without a recheck trigger silently becomes stale advice.
alternatives_rejected: A generic 'conditions may change' (unactionable).
building_agnostic_how: Recheck horizon derives from the modality's observed volatility in that building's data, not a fixed interval.
key_steps: 1) Derive recheck horizon from the modality's volatility. 2) State the switch condition. 3) Put both on the record.
acceptance_criteria: Every recommendation carries evidence time, recheck point and switch trigger.
verify: Probe a recommendation.
notes: [DONE 2026-08-25] evidence/recheck.py, appended after persona formatting to RECOMMENDATIONS only -- a historical figure has no expiry and a recheck line on one is noise. Three parts: EVIDENCE TIME (when the readings were taken, never when the answer was written), a RECHECK POINT derived from the modality's own volatility via the freshness policy (one source for both, so a building that tunes its limits gets consistent advice instead of a second table that drifts), and a SWITCH TRIGGER that NAMES the runner-up -- 'come back and ask again' puts the work back on the reader, which is what the advice was meant to remove. Evidence time is the OLDEST contributing observation: a recommendation resting on four sensors is only as current as its stalest input, and reporting the freshest would overstate exactly the thing this line bounds. UNDECLARED VOLATILITY IS STATED, NEVER INVENTED -- a confident expiry on an unknown quantity is the same fabrication as a confident reading. WIRING IT FOUND TWO THINGS: the dossier carries no evidence timestamp at all (the recommendation lane genuinely could not say when its readings were taken, so the line falls back to the evidence record), and the deliberate lane was ranking NOTHING because 235 of 236 noise sensors were stale behind a fresh-looking table max. 19 tests.

title: Accessibility as a hard filter
objective: Treat accessibility requirements as hard constraints: never label a route step-free unless verified, and recommend neither option if both fail.
why: R-11, stated in three catalogues. An unverified step-free claim can strand someone — the highest real-world harm in the whole question bank.
alternatives_rejected: Ranking accessible options higher (a preference, not a filter — it still returns inaccessible options as answers); inferring step-free from the presence of a lift (a lift may be out of service).
building_agnostic_how: Accessibility attributes are per-building triples; the filter is generic and a building that declares none returns the honest empty result.
key_steps: 1) Accessibility as a hard admission constraint. 2) Require verified status. 3) Return nothing with an explanation rather than an unverified option.
acceptance_criteria: Unverified accessibility is never labelled accessible; both-fail returns an explained empty result.
verify: Fixture with unverified and out-of-service routes.
notes: [DONE 2026-08-21] orchestrator/services/evidence/accessibility.py filter_options(). FILTERS rather than ranks - a ranked list still returns inaccessible options and is read as a list of answers. Unverified is EXCLUDED, not caveated: a caveat on a route is read after the person has decided to take it. An out-of-service dependency is checked BEFORE verification, because a verified route through a failed lift is not a verified route today and the verification record is the thing most likely to mislead (it was true when written). An empty result is a valid explained answer naming the assistance contact. A question with NO accessibility requirement is not filtered at all, so the hard filter cannot quietly narrow ordinary questions. 24 tests (shared file with T40).

title: Omitted-criteria reporting
objective: Report which requested criteria were omitted and why, using the catalogues' template.
why: R-9. A ranking that silently drops a criterion the user asked for answers a different question than the one asked, and looks complete doing it.
alternatives_rejected: Silently dropping unavailable criteria (the current behaviour on some lanes).
building_agnostic_how: Requested-vs-used criteria are tracked structurally; the criteria themselves come from the question and the building's modalities.
key_steps: 1) Track requested-vs-used criteria. 2) Render the template. 3) Populate omitted_criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Every omitted criterion is named with one of the three reasons.
verify: Ask for a criterion the building lacks; assert it is reported.
notes: Built as orchestrator/services/evidence/omissions.py; populates the existing OmittedCriterion model and EvidenceRecord.omitted_criteria. Reports all FIVE OmissionReason members in the catalogues' three-word template shape -- the two refinements (not_instrumented, inadequate_coverage) earn their place because they carry different remedies. Ordering is argued in classify(): not_instrumented first (no governance route exists), restricted BEFORE missing (they look identical to a user and lead to opposite actions). facts_from_ranking() reads what the deliberation lane already tracks (constraints vs scored modalities) and takes plain dicts so a second lane can reuse it. TWO findings: (1) an empty declared-modality list must mean 'not stated', not 'nothing instrumented', or every criterion is condemned on any caller that has not wired the list yet -- pinned by a test; (2) the template's own wording contains 'because', so every omission line is a causal sentence syntactically and T33 would have rewritten them -- caught here by a cross-module test rather than in production, and fixed by widening the causal guard's meta-cause vocabulary. 23 tests, all passing. [AUDIT 2026-08-23] Marked done with acceptance criteria about live behaviour, and the live pipeline never imports this module — reachability audit found only tests and the evidence package's own __init__ referencing it: dossier.py has 0 references to omissions; the deliberate lane's exclusions never become OmittedCriterion entries on the record. [WIRED 2026-08-23, Wave A] The deliberate lane's dossier coverage_excluded entries become OmittedCriterion on the record; reason mapping is conservative (unrecognised prose -> INADEQUATE_COVERAGE, the weakest claim).

title: Recurring time-of-day windows
objective: Add an (hour_start, hour_end, weekdays) mask alongside the date range, pushed into adapters as a HOUR() predicate.
why: Verified absent: sql_agent._build_uuid_union_query builds only ts BETWEEN start AND end, and _sanitize_datetime accepts nothing else. One shared change unlocks night water baselines, after-hours energy, 'full by lunchtime' patterns and after-hours conditioning across several categories at once. config/recipes.yaml already declares a night_leak_threshold that nothing can currently evaluate at night.
alternatives_rejected: Per-question special cases (multiplies the surface and drifts); post-filtering in Python (moves large result sets over the wire for no reason).
building_agnostic_how: The hour mask is parsed from the question; the DEFAULT window comes from the building's declared occupied hours, never a hardcoded 08-18.
key_steps: 1) Parse the mask from the question. 2) Push into each adapter's builder as a dialect hint. 3) Default the window from the building's declared occupied hours, not a constant.
acceptance_criteria: Night/after-hours windows answerable on every adapter; no building literal; the night leak recipe evaluates against night data.

title: Water: hot/cold split and leak persistence
objective: Split water into hot/cold modalities and add a night-minimum persistence detector for slow leaks.
why: Verified: the existing water_flow_leak recipe compares a single reading against a night threshold with no notion of night and no persistence, and the schedule_violation detector's 0.5x-median threshold means a genuine 0.3 L/min leak on a 12 L/min main is NEVER flagged. Also absence_guard._MODALITY_ALIASES omits water, so a false 'no water sensors' claim would go uncaught.
alternatives_rejected: Tuning the existing single-reading threshold (cannot distinguish a leak from legitimate low flow without persistence); a new bespoke leak service (the detector framework already exists).
building_agnostic_how: The persistence detector derives its floor from each meter's own history, as the existing detectors do; the hot/cold split is a config entry.
key_steps: 1) Hot/cold modality split in config. 2) minimum_flow_persistence detector over N nights. 3) Add water to the absence guard aliases. 4) Route leak episodes to URGENT dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: A simulated slow leak is detected; legitimate low flow is not; single-meter buildings say they cannot localise.
verify: Synthetic leak fixture + a no-leak control.
notes: minimum_flow_persistence() added to anomaly/detectors.py and dispatched from scanner.py for FLOW_MODALITIES. Detects by PERSISTENCE, not magnitude: a 0.3 L/min leak on a 12 L/min main is 2.5% of normal flow, so schedule_violation's 0.5x-in-hours-median rule needs 6 L/min before it fires -- no threshold tuning bridges that, which is why this is a new detector. Requires BOTH a night minimum above the meter's OWN idle level and N consecutive nights; the floor is max(3 x MAD of night minima, 0.5% of daytime median), both derived from that meter's history, so a 2 L/min trickle meter and a 200 L/min main each get their own. Trailing run only, so a repaired leak is not reported as current. meters_on_this_stream drives an explicit localisable flag -- a single-metered building can tell you it is leaking and not where, and omitting that sends someone to the wrong floor. VERIFIED against the acceptance criteria: 0.3-on-12 leak detected (score 5.0, high); clean meter, one late night, 2-night run, repaired leak, brand-new meter and flat meter all silent; a building with a genuine 4 L/min continuous night draw is silent but IS flagged when 0.3 is added on top. MODALITY SPLIT: water_flow_hot + water_flow_chilled added to config/saturation_modalities.yaml using CONFIRMED Brick 1.4 classes; NO cold entry, because Brick 1.4 has no domestic-cold sensor class and declaring a generic Water_Meter to be cold would assert what that meter measures without support. title: Golden baseline + regression gate over all 1,580 questions
objective: Capture every answer the system gives today across the full 1,580-question bank, with its evidence, and gate every later V6 task against it: each changed answer must classify as improved, unchanged, intended-tightening (naming the gate and reason), or REGRESSION.
why: V6's gates are restrictive by design, so some answers WILL change. Without a baseline there is no way to tell an intended tightening (an answer that was never supported by its evidence) from a regression (an answer that was correct and now is not) — and the two look identical in an aggregate coverage number. This must be captured BEFORE any V6 code lands, because a baseline taken afterwards has already absorbed whatever it was meant to detect.
alternatives_rejected: Relying on the unit suite (it tests components, not answers, and cannot see a coverage change); comparing coverage percentages only (an aggregate hides which questions moved, and equal totals can conceal offsetting gains and losses); reviewing changed answers by hand (1,580 questions x 53 tasks is not reviewable, and the V4/V5 history shows manual review is exactly where false results enter).
building_agnostic_how: Baseline is captured per building and compared per building; the gate compares a building against ITSELF, never against another.
key_steps: 1) Replay all 1,580 questions on a healthy stack; archive answer + evidence + status per question per building. 2) Differ: classify each changed answer into the four buckets. 3) Require every tightening to name the gate that fired and its reason; an answer that got worse with NO gate firing is a regression and blocks the task. 4) Wire into run_all_graders.py.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline archived for all 1,580 questions before T01 lands; the gate classifies every changed answer; regressions=0 is a hard pass condition for every subsequent task; a deliberately introduced regression is caught by the gate.
verify: Capture the baseline, then break something on purpose (e.g. narrow a referent) and confirm the gate reports it as a regression rather than a tightening.
notes: MVP-0 — runs BEFORE V6-T01. Grading is only valid if the stack was healthy for the whole run (CLAUDE.md); quarantine degraded rows rather than scoring them. GATE BUILT: scripts/baseline_regression_gate.py classifies every changed answer as unchanged / live-drift / reworded / route-changed / tightened / loosened / improved / REGRESSION / dropped, blocking on REGRESSION and DROPPED, exit code 1 on failure. The building is live and the provider is nondeterministic at temp 0 (measured in BUG-184), so a text comparison would report near-total change over 1,580 questions and gate nothing.
